<Update label="2026-10-28" tags={["API"]}>

### API

**Behavior change**

- `POST /app-fees/{wallet}/claim` and `POST /execute/permits` (with `kind: "claim"`): the claim `recipient` is now validated as a payout target before any balance is debited. Recipients that are Relay deposit addresses, the zero address, well-known burn addresses, or otherwise unresolvable return `400` with `message: "Invalid destination chain and/or recipient"` — on `/app-fees/{wallet}/claim` before authorization is issued, and on `/execute/permits` before the balance is debited. Previously only address-format was checked, and invalid recipients were accepted at authorization and failed later in payout, leaving the balance unavailable. Properly addressed EVM wallet recipients continue to work unchanged. See [App Fees — withdrawing your off-chain balance](/features/app-fees#how-to-withdraw-your-off-chain-balance).
- All authenticated endpoints: rate-limit and burst-allowance budgets are now scoped to the App rather than to the individual API key, so every active and rotated key in an App shares one budget per route. Previously, each key received its own counters, which allowed additional or rotated keys to multiply effective capacity. Elevated `/authorize` buckets now key on `(App, wallet)` with an aggregate per-App ceiling (previously `(API key, wallet)` with a per-API-key ceiling). Anonymous fallbacks, user/session rules, and pre-authentication `/access-tokens` limits are unchanged. See [Apps, API keys, and Rate Limits](/references/api/api-keys#default-rate-limits).

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-26" tags={["UI Kit", "Hooks"]}>

### RelayKit

**UI Kit `12.0.6`** — Patch

- `useTokenPrice` and `queryTokenPrice` now call `GET /currencies/token/price/v2`, and `data.price` is a decimal string instead of a number. - `useRelayConfig` and `queryRelayConfig` are removed. They called `GET /config/v2`, which retires with no successor on January 28, 2027. Stop calling the endpoint and drop any code that read its response. ([`ab44c08`](https://github.com/relayprotocol/relay-kit/commit/ab44c08))

Parse it with `Number()` where you do arithmetic and keep the string for display and storage; the Swap and Onramp widgets already do. `GET /currencies/token/price` is deprecated from October 30, 2026 and retires on January 28, 2027. <Update label="2026-10-23" tags={["Dashboard"]}>

### Dashboard

**Added**

- The Dashboard now organizes your integration into Apps. Each App contains API keys
  and one configuration that all of its keys use. The configuration includes rate limits,
  features, the webhook, IP restrictions, allowed origins, the fee sponsorship wallet, and app
  fees. Give each product or environment its own App, so that every key for it behaves the same
  way. For more information, see [API keys](/references/api/api-keys).
- You can now rotate an API key without a change to its configuration. Create a
  replacement key in the same App. Change your integration to use the replacement key. Then
  deactivate the old key.

**Changed**

- Each API key from before this release is now a separate App. Each App has the
  same name and configuration as its key, so your integration does not need changes. The API
  Keys page is now the Apps page, and links to `/api-keys` redirect to `/apps`.

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-21" tags={["API"]}>

### API

**Breaking**

- `POST /currencies/v1` and `POST /currencies/v2`: `limit` must now be an **integer ≥ 1**. Values of `0`, negative numbers, and non-integers return `400` instead of being silently accepted. `POST /currencies/v2` continues to enforce its existing `maximum: 100` and default of `20`.
- `POST /currencies/v1` and `POST /currencies/v2`: `term` is capped at **256 characters**. Longer values return `400`.
- `POST /currencies/v1` and `POST /currencies/v2`: requests with `useExternalSearch: true` now require a non-empty `chainIds` array. Requests that omit `chainIds` or send `[]` with external search enabled return `400`.

**Behavior change**

- `POST /currencies/v1`: unfiltered requests that omit `limit` now return a default of **20** currency groups. Requests that include any filter (`defaultList`, `chainIds`, `term`, `address`, `symbol`, `groupID`, `tokens`, `verified`, or `depositAddressOnly`) or an explicit `limit` are unaffected. If your integration relied on receiving the full curated list in one call, send an explicit `limit` or a filter.

**Added**

- `POST /currencies/v1` and `POST /currencies/v2`: `symbol` and `groupID` are now documented request fields — optional string filters by currency symbol and currency group ID. Behavior is unchanged from how these filters were previously accepted.

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-15" tags={["API"]}>

### API

**Behavior change**

- `POST /quote` and `POST /quote/v2`: the per-key rate limit on elevated keys is raised from **10 requests per second** to **50 requests per second** across both endpoints. Default keys are unchanged at 50 requests per minute. See [Elevated Rate Limits](/references/api/api-keys#elevated-rate-limits).

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-14" tags={["Protocol"]}>

### Protocol

**Behavior change**

- On October 26, 2026 at 10 AM ET, Relay starts routing through the new contracts on all supported chains, and `contracts.erc20Router` and `contracts.approvalProxy` in Get Chains switch to them. Both pairs stay live during the transition, so if you validate contract addresses, allow both. Token approvals go to the new approval proxy, so a returning user approves once more ([migration notes](/references/api/api_resources/contract-addresses#migrating-to-the-new-router)).

**Added**

- Router 3.2 and a new approval proxy are deployed on all supported EVM chains. Most chains use router `0x0729e2a4716d9f7dd17858d5d504426d228697f7` and approval proxy `0x5567954cd026cebfe486062cb75848e0f1c12e58`; Cronos, Linea, Mantle and Metis use router `0x6328ea02d28131e58b28e55c6258258a30d90e05` and approval proxy `0xe4dfbd5e6784db1058124e2c87554c0591f0fb7b`. [Get Chains](/references/api/get-chains) lists the pair for each chain under `contracts["v3.2"]`.

**Changed**

- The router's `SolverCallExecuted` event logs a 32 byte hash of the call data instead of the call data. On the approval proxy, the Permit2 witness includes `msgValue`, `permitTransferAndMulticall` (ERC-2612) no longer has a nonce in its permit struct, and `permit3009TransferAndMulticall` takes an extra `multicallSignatures` argument, because ERC-3009 permits need a MulticallAuthorization signature that clients opt into with `useMulticallAuthorization`. Nothing changes for integrations that only use the transaction data returned by the quote API.

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-13" tags={["API"]}>

### API

**Added**

- `GET /metrics/usage`: the new optional `appId` query parameter filters usage by App — the durable identity for an integration, which persists across API key rotation. Accepts one or more `app_id_<uuid>` values as a comma-separated list (OR-matched, trimmed, canonicalized to lowercase, deduplicated). Requires `x-dev-portal-key`; a plain `x-api-key` cannot use this filter and attempts return `403`. OR-matches with `apiKey` and `apiKeyId`, and the three filters share a combined cap of **50** values before Apps expand to their keys. Every supplied ID must belong to the authenticating integrator; malformed IDs return `400` and unknown or foreign IDs return `403` for the entire request. The filter resolves every current credential under an App — including inactive keys — and an owned App without credentials returns an empty `metrics` array.
- `GET /metrics/usage`: each row in the response `metrics` array now includes a nullable **`appId`** alongside `apiKey` and `apiKeyId`, carrying the current App the key is attributed to. App attribution is resolved at read time, so hard-deleting a credential drops it from App totals and a reassigned credential attributes all of its retained usage to its current App. Retention windows are unchanged: 24h minutely, 7d hourly, 14d daily. See [API keys and Rate Limits](/references/api/api-keys).

</Update>

<Update label="2026-10-12" tags={["API"]}>

### API

**Breaking**

- `POST /quote` and `POST /quote/v2`: the `details.fallbackType` field is removed from the response. It was only populated when a canonical+ fallback route served the quote; with that path removed, the field no longer appears on any response.

**Deprecated**

- `POST /quote`, `POST /quote/v2`, and `POST /price`: the `useExternalLiquidity` and `useFallbacks` request fields are now accepted but ignored. The canonical+ bridging path and the fallback-route path they selected have been removed from the quote engine. Both fields are marked `deprecated` in the request schema and can be dropped from your integration. Callers that previously sent `useExternalLiquidity: true` now receive a standard quote instead of a `400`.
- `GET /config` and `GET /config/v2`: the per-chain-combination `supportsExternalLiquidity` field is marked `deprecated` and now always returns `false`. The field remains in the response shape for backwards compatibility — treat it as a constant and remove any branching on its value.

</Update>
